messages:
incident-bot: PAGED @oncall-sre — sudden 8x 5xx spike on /v1/generate in us-west-2 starting ~2143658690, sustained for ~2m. Multiple client IPs, same UA pattern. Suspect: proxy/robot farm + credential stuffing. Alerting: high token churn, elevated CPU on GPU-pool-3 :rotating_light:

mike.h: I'm on it. Can someone dump the top client IPs and user agents?

sara.j: grabbing netflow + edge logs now. running quick aggregation: `jq '.requests | group_by(.ip) | .[] | {ip: .[0].ip, count: length}'`

adele: shout if you want me to kick off a mass WAF rule. I can geo-block a few high-noise regions temporarily.

oncall-sre: please hold on WAF until we confirm risk to customers. First do live rate-slicing on anonymous keys + reduce bursts. Add token-level throttles for new keys from same IP cluster.

leo: infra-bot, can you push a temporary rate-limit change? Need to cut anon-unauthed burst to 6rps per IP and global per-key to 30r/min for 1h.

infra-bot: deploying rate-slice rule now. Preview: `rate_limit: {scope: ip, limit: 6, window: 1s}` and `api_key_rate: {scope: key, limit: 30, window: 60s}`. Rolling to edge in 30s.

security-bot: detected credential-stuffing signature: repeated login attempts + header rotator (UA pattern libcurl/++). Suggest blocking known proxy ranges and enabling CAPTCHA challenge on auth endpoints.

mike.h: rolled rate-limits at 2143658760. Observing 60% drop in offending traffic within 40s. Still seeing multiple failed auth attempts.

adele: starting a targeted WAF rule for the top 5 CIDR blocks that correlate to the spike. Action: challenge for all POSTs to /v1/auth and block for /v1/embed for anonymous. Duration 1h.

oncall-sre: good. Apply geo caps for cn, ru, kz for anonymous traffic only. Do not affect authenticated existing customers. Add a snackbar notice for degraded perf to CS.

cs-ops: noted. I'll draft a short customer message: "We are experiencing increased automated traffic; some requests may be rate-limited. If you see new 429s, please contact support."

incident-bot: deploy-bot reports: 2 config updates applied (rate-slice + WAF targeted blocks) at 2143658795. No rollbacks.

leo: dashboards: 5xx back down to baseline in 3m from change, token churn reduced 45%. But a small percentage of legitimate long-poll customers on shared NATs got 429s.

mike.h: mitigation tradeoff accepted. For impacted customers we can create exceptions (whitelist by X-Client-ID). Opening a short-lived exception ticket per request.

security-bot: running follow-up scan on credential-stuffing source IPs. Recommend adding IP reputation feeds to block list. Also create a rule to detect header-rotator UA signatures and escalate.

infra-bot: added a temporary anomaly rule to drop requests with >100 requests/min from any single token over 30s. Will revert automatically after 2h.

adele: WAF stats: blocked ~12M requests in 45m, prevented ~3.4M auth attempts. False-positive rate ~0.3% based on sampled logs.

cs-ops: CS team notified customers with heavy NATs; offering whitelist & guidance. No major enterprise SLAs hit, a few dev accounts saw degraded throughput and 429s.

oncall-sre: handing off to night oncall @mike.h for monitoring; mitigation rules expire 2h from now by policy. If we see recurrence, escalate to sec-priority and permanent CIDR blocks.

mike.h: acknowledged. I'll keep an eye and collect a short post-incident summary with timestamps and actions. tagging @security-bot @infra-bot for follow-up runbook updates. :thumbsup:
